defect.evidence_quote: This case presents the question of the degree of immunity accorded a defendant police officer in a damages action under 42 U. S. C. § 1983 when it is alleged that the officer caused the plaintiffs to be unconstitutionally arrested by presenting a judge with a complaint and a supporting affidavit which failed to establish probable cause.
defect.problem: The disclosed opinion supports a warrant-affidavit probable-cause/qualified-immunity case, but it does not disclose any Franks doctrine issue, false-statement/omission challenge, or internal evidence explaining why this belongs on 'Franks Challenges'.
defect.proposed_fix: Remove the Franks Challenges home role unless the corpus supplies a Franks-page rationale tying Malley to affidavit challenges; otherwise retitle the relationship as a general warrant-affidavit/probable-cause cross-reference.

reasons: The opinion text frames the case as qualified immunity for an officer who submitted a warrant affidavit allegedly lacking probable cause.
No disclosed file contains the Franks Challenges page content or a Franks-specific linkage.
residual_risks: A separate internal Franks page might justify this as cross-doctrine, but that evidence is not disclosed here.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: If retained, label it narrowly as related only by warrant-affidavit probable-cause review, not as a Franks holding.

reasons: The opinion states that objective reasonableness defines qualified immunity for an officer whose warrant request allegedly caused an unconstitutional arrest.

The opinion states that immunity is lost only where the warrant application is so lacking in indicia of probable cause as to render official belief unreasonable, and elsewhere says defendants are not immune if no reasonably competent officer would have concluded a warrant should issue.
The opinion rejects absolute immunity for the warrant-applying officer.
The opinion is centrally about qualified immunity under § 1983 for an officer applying for a warrant.
The opinion expressly applies Harlow and Leon objective-reasonableness standards to define the qualified immunity accorded in this warrant-application context.
Lake identity identifies the court as U.S. Supreme Court and court_level as scotus, supporting the 'Binding — SCOTUS' weight label.
